ee2aa7a522fa96110e13.text: 1. You better stay home. The possibility of you getting sick scares me.

4dab0a4fffed08065717.text:
(The verb “scarefs” is used to state the unpleasant emotion towards the possibility of
getting sick. Stating an emotion is a way in convincing someone.)
2. No, Noel. I strongly disagree. You should follow what I tell you.

dac39cf2574c2f5fa258.text: (The verb disagree states the stand of the speaker. Emphasizing a stand is a good way in influencing someone to agree with your ideas.) A. MODAL VERBS

b51a5b6647e6fd1dd35c.text: In Module 3, you have learned that modal verbs have different uses. The modals given below are verbs that express suggestion or recommendation which is an effective way to convince or persuade. To further clarify the difference of each modal, they are arranged from weakest to strongest in terms of expressing a suggestion or recommendation. Furthermore, the table shows their functions and examples.

83251e64110f059dfe23.text: Type of  Functions Examples  Verb     Modals    Could   It is used to give a suggestion which a person may or may not follow. I suggest you play with your brother and sister or you could join me pray for your Tatay’s safety. (The modal could is used to give a suggestion that the person could join the speaker in praying.) Should   It is also used to give a suggestion but more insistent than the modal could. No, Noel. I strongly disagree. You should follow what I tell you. (The modal should is used to suggest that the person needs to follow what the speaker tells.)
rows: It is used to give a suggestion which a person may or may not follow.
I suggest you play with your brother and sister or you could join me pray for your Tatay’s safety. (The modal could is used to give a suggestion that the person could join the speaker in praying.)
It is also used to give a suggestion but more insistent than the modal could.
No, Noel. I strongly disagree. You should follow what I tell you. (The modal should is used to suggest that the person needs to follow what the speaker tells.)
It is used to formally give an advice or a recommendation usually coming from an expert.
The Department of Health (DOH) recommends that people ought to stay at home so that they will not get sick. (The modal ought to is used to formally suggest that staying at home is important.)
It is used to give a recommendation by presenting the possible negative consequence if the advice is not followed.

During the Enhanced Community Quarantine (ECQ), you had better wear your mask in public places or the police will arrest you. (The modal had better is used since the possible negative consequence, the police will arrest you, is presented to serve as a warning.)
It is used to show a strong obligation that needs to be followed.

The government must control the people’s movement in public to stop the spread of the virus. (The modal must is used to express the strong obligation of the government in taking action against the spread of the virus.)
ca601284b3e09e8039c1.text: Ought to It is used to formally give an advice or a recommendation usually coming from an expert. The Department of Health (DOH) recommends that people ought to stay at home so that they will not get sick. (The modal ought to is used to formally suggest that staying at home is important.) Had better It is used to give a recommendation by presenting the possible negative consequence if the advice is not followed. During the Enhanced Community Quarantine (ECQ), you had better wear your mask in public places or the police will arrest you. (The modal had better is used since the possible negative consequence, the police will arrest you, is presented to serve as a warning.) Must It is used to show a strong obligation that needs to be followed. The government must control the people’s movement in public to stop the spread of the virus. (The modal must is used to express the strong obligation of the government in taking action against the spread of the virus.)

28c7c5ac4e176436178d.text: Now, take a look at another paragraph that uses adjectives together with the verbs that you have learned in Lesson 1. These range of adjectives and verbs are commonly used in writing a persuasive paragraph.

5d83fd13a98ee62c21a1.text: We all know that good nutrition is important, but the pandemic definitely made us realize that we must practice eating healthy at all times. As always mentioned by health professionals, we ought to eat a well-balanced diet accompanied with regular exercise. Absolutely, this is essential in maintaining physical health as well as mental health. Without this, we are completely not safe from getting the deadly virus. So, why wait for this frightening moment to happen? Start eating nutritious food and motivate others to do the same.

a18704cf55abc30ef825.text: Now, take note of the word strongly in the choices. This word is an adverb that emphasizes your reactions. You will learn more examples of this type and how to use them in this lesson.

559c929c277ce873e3d8.text: In Lesson 1 and Lesson 2, you were introduced to using a range of verbs and adjectives in expressing your emotions and opinions. This time you will learn about adverbs.

f44bf26e48ce5ac0fe05.text: The sentences below are based on the Story of the Aged Mother. Try to compare them and take note of their differences.

labels.text: I agree that old people must
The farmer in the story was

715429a8f2e5091f6681.text: I agree that old people must  be respected and protected.  The farmer in the story was  happy that her mother saved  the people.

labels.text: The farmer in the story was

aefcfde1f17a2693397d.text: strongly  agree that old  people must be respected and  protected.  The farmer in the story was  really  happy that her mother  saved the people.

4d829b2ee492fa859d54.text: What is the difference between sentence 1 and sentence 2? How about sentence 3 and sentence 4? Which sentences sound more convincing to you?

1e2c8cb01961a389cab2.text: Notice that sentences 2 contains the words “strongly”. This word gives a higher emotional degree on the verb agree. Also, take note that sentence 4 contains the word “really”. This word emphasizes that the happiness felt by the farmer is more intense than the happiness expressed in sentence 1.

d71b0a9e10d76ac99bb4.text: The words “strongly” and “really” are examples of adverbs. They describe verbs, adjectives, and another adverb. There are many types of adverbs but in this lesson, you will focus on adverbs that can give emphasis on your responses and reactions. They are called adverbs of opinion.

00f9172f8256af22aa40.text: This type of adverbs emphasizes the intensity of your stand or opinion. They help clarify your belief about a certain issue. The following are the commonly used adverbs of opinion:

rows: Owing to good luck or favor

f6f0ac737567ae17c0cb.text: Take note on how some of the adverbs above are used in the following sentences:

4a0e36675727467a9e7a.text: 1. Clearly, the farmer in the story loved her old mother. He showed this by

55e535521f3d02bf9fd7.text: protecting and hiding his mother from the cruel governor. (The adverb clearly emphasizes that the farmer’s love to his old mother is very clear in the story. The adverb clearly is placed at the beginning of the sentence. This means that they can be placed at the beginning of sentences and are followed with a comma.)

ab51d35a7bf39482c3f2.text: 2. Minors and senior citizens must stay at home during the pandemic. We

9e4447e94c523ff1c911.text: definitely need to follow this health measure to protect them. (The adverb definitely emphasizes the stand of the speaker that he or she is certain that the health measure must be followed. The adverb definitely is placed before the verb need. This means that they can also be placed before the main verb.)

1901a7b5ef485a95b8d3.text: 3. Filipinos’ sense of respect to old people is evidently shown on how they protect

987a3d9710f3d0338ed6.text: and care for their old family members. (The adverb evidently emphasizes the observation of the speaker that Filipinos’ sense of respect to old people is clearly seen on how they treat old family members. The adverb is placed in between the word are and doing. This means that they can be placed between an auxiliary verb and a main verb.)

2bd61abc0b427c931f85.text: Furthermore, adverbs of opinion can also be in a form of phrases. The table below shows some of the commonly used phrases that function as an adverb of opinion.

c9ce9b90a9ba62b51303.text: From my view To be frank In fact In my opinion Without a doubt

0077f330c08cabf2e476.text: Take a look at how they are used in a sentence.

db16784d3470a9692f9a.text: Filipinos are really respectful and polite to old people. Without a doubt, filial piety has been always part of our culture. (The phrase without a doubt shows the firm feelings of the speaker that filial piety or respect to elders has always been a part of our culture. The phrase is placed at the beginning of the sentence. This means that they are usually placed at the beginning of a sentence and followed by a comma.)

2aa53a333c3fdfcbfea8.text: Adverbs of opinion can also help emphasize the ideas in your paragraph especially if you want to convince readers about your opinion to an issue.

1ec7ebb4aa7b362d9495.text: This module is written to suit your language needs as a Grade 8 learner. It is here to help you master skills that will allow you to appropriately and responsibly communicate your thoughts and feelings especially in this time when different information and issues arise. Hence, there is a need for you to learn how to properly respond and express your opinions on issues that you may experience in society.

d1149152ce1e8352003e.text: Have you ever encountered any issues that you want to give your opinion? Were you able to communicate your feelings clearly? How?

c93cb41fff8654edd3e8.text: Perhaps, you have tried doing it in different ways; however, there might also be moments that made you feel that it is difficult to express your ideas especially in English. Thus, this module will help you learn different ways to communicate your emotions and reactions to certain issues.

d1b3a0257d2abdda33a5.text: The Most Essential Learning Competency (MELC) covered in this module is use a range of verbs, adjectives, and adverbs to convey emotional response or reactions to an issue to persuade. Objectives:

76cdd99c0f8c97cee69b.text: As a learner of this module, you are expected to:

68ce74982c42b45bd1bf.text:
•
identify the appropriate verbs, adjectives, and adverbs used in conveying emotions
and opinions for persuasion;
•
use appropriate verbs, adjectives, and adverbs in expressing emotions and
opinions for persuasion; and
•
write a persuasive paragraph using verbs, adjectives, and adverbs.
